fail_samples.text_head: Quarterly Investment Update September 2026 Market overview Broader global and Australian equities eked out modest gains in the September quarter, rising +1.5% (in A$ terms) and +1.3% respectively. However, global listed infrastructure declined -7.0% as higher Global listed infrastructure borrowing costs weighed on the asset class, particularly the more interest rate-sensitive subsectors. In response to declined as higher re-emerging inflation pressures linked to the conflict in the borrowing costs weighed Middle East and the war between Russia and Ukraine, the US on the asset class, Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate for the first time since 2023. particularly the more Regulated utilities, which make up more than half of the interest rate-sensitive asset class, were among the worst affected by higher costs of capital. These businesses can carry considerable debt regulated utilities. because of their reliable income streams from essential services. Electric Utilities, in particular, had one of their weakest quarters in recent memory, as higher bond yields made their steady dividends comparatively less attractive. Backlash against data centres added to the pressure. US utilities in states that welcome data centres performed relatively well, while those in states facing considerable political and community resistance, including data centre moratoriums, fell sharply. Passenger transportation subsectors also declined, pressured by weaker travel demand and rising interest rates. Airports fell sharply, led by Mexican operators amid continued weakness in passenger traffic, and European operators posted steep losses. Record fuel prices added to concerns, with fears that higher airfares could weigh on travel demand. Portfolio performance Argo Infrastructure’s portfolio declined -6.5% (in A$ terms) in the September quarter, marginally outperforming the benchmark index. Performance was bolstered by an overweight position in Japanese electric utility Kansai Electric. The company announced its first major increase in corporate electricity rates in more than a decade, boosting optimism that utilities across the country could pass rising costs on to customers and contributing to a broad rally. An overweight allocation to Indian port operator JSW Infrastructure also added to relative returns after it successfully raised capital to fund its plans to more than double its port capacity by 2028. Conversely, an overweight position in Mexican airport operator ASUR weighed on performance, as Mexican airports declined broadly amid continued weakness in passenger traffic. 3 months 1 year 3 years (p.a.) fail_samples.text_head: NTA AND INVESTMENT UPDATE September 2026 The CDO share price and NTA went ex-dividend on 29 September 2026 for the 7.5 cps fully franked final dividend, resulting in the post-tax NTA being $2.137 at the end of September. Before the dividend was paid, the post-tax NTA was $2.212, in line with the $2.21 issue price of the SPP and placement. Fund Performance Cadence Opportunities Fund was down 4.9% in September, compared to the All Ordinaries Accumulation Index which was down 2.5% for the month. For the first quarter of the financial year, the portfolio was down 2.4%, compared to the All Ordinaries Accumulation Index which was up 1.0% for the quarter. CDO’s share price over the past quarter, including dividends and franking, was up 8.1%, and for the year was up 32.0%. The largest detractors from performance during the first quarter were Lindian Resources, Guzman Y Gomez, EchoIQ, Pro Medicus, Life360, and Liontown. The top contributors were Turaco Gold, CSL, Kantra Copper, Many Peaks Minerals, Generation Development Group, Metals X and Ringcentral. Lindian Resources is developing its Kangankunde rare earth project in Malawi which it expects to ramp up through 2027. During the period, Lindian’s share price fell 47% following two key developments: the announcement of an offtake agreement with French downstream specialist Carestar and proposed amendments to the Malawi Mining Code. CDO reduced its exposure to Lindian during the period. We maintain a position with the view that the government will act rationally, and the proposed mine will proceed. EchoIQ specialises in artificial intelligence solutions for cardiovascular diagnostics. During the period, the fund re-entered EchoIQ after trading it successfully earlier in 2026. The fund entered this position prior to FDA approval which did not occur in the first instance. A meeting with the FDA in connection with EIQ’s appeal is expected to occur within the next 30 days. Having successfully shorted Guzman Y Gomez during the last financial year, the fund closed its remaining short position during this quarter. Core positions in Turaco Gold, CSL, Kantra Copper and Many Peaks performed well during the period. Interest rates set by the Reserve Bank and longer-term yields set by the bond market, rose substantially over the past quarter. Some of the factors driving higher interest rates are global government deficits and the flow- on impact that it has on inflation through elevated government spending. This backdrop provides a tailwind for gold positions in the fund. Turaco Gold and Many Peaks are two such examples. Our top performing stock for the quarter, Turaco Gold is advancing towards the release of its Definitive Feasibility Study (DFS), a key deliverable prior to first production, with the company also considered a takeover target for mid and large cap gold companies in the region. Many Peaks continues to return high grade gold hits from drilling at its Ferke project in Côte d’Ivoire, which will enable it to expand upon its recently released maiden gold Resource of 1.3Moz. Higher interest rates impacting valuations have also created opportunities to initiate new long positions. Some stocks that were once expensive and did not meet our investment criteria began to meet our criteria during the period following abrupt sell-offs. CSL is one such example. The investment portfolio remains diversified across a range of alternative asset classes, with the investment team continuing to focus on identifying opportunities that can deliver attractive risk-adjusted returns for shareholders. A notable contributor to the investment portfolio performance during the month was Slater and Gordon in the WAM Alternative Assets private equity portfolio, which experienced a valuation uplift following continued robust business performance. Slater and Gordon is one of Australia’s leading consumer law firms, with a long history across personal injury law, class actions, commercial litigation and employment law. The business is owned through Allegro Fund IV, following Allegro’s 2023 take-private of the formerly ASX-listed company. The investment reflects Allegro’s Active Complex Transformation strategy, which focuses on partnering with businesses that have strong underlying foundations and creating value through operational improvement. Since acquiring Slater and Gordon, Allegro has focused on revitalising the business through improved workflows, stronger processes and technology enablement. For the WAM Alternative Assets investment portfolio, Slater and Gordon represents a private equity investment where value can be created through disciplined operational change over time.
